title: Dynamic Programming Fundamentals
description: Learn how Dynamic Programming solves complex problems efficiently by reusing previously computed results.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Many recursive algorithms repeatedly solve the same subproblems multiple times.

This repeated computation wastes processing time and significantly reduces efficiency.

Dynamic Programming improves performance by storing previously computed results and reusing them whenever the same subproblem appears again.

sections.title: The Core Idea of Dynamic Programming
sections.content:
Dynamic Programming breaks complex problems into smaller overlapping subproblems.

Instead of recalculating solutions repeatedly, the algorithm stores intermediate results in memory.

Whenever the same subproblem is encountered again, the stored answer can be reused immediately.

sections.title: Overlapping Subproblems
sections.content:
A problem contains overlapping subproblems when the same smaller computations appear repeatedly.

Traditional recursive solutions may solve identical subproblems many times unnecessarily.

Dynamic Programming avoids this repetition by saving computed answers and reusing them throughout execution.

sections.title: Memoization vs Tabulation
sections.content:
Memoization stores results during recursive execution. When a recursive call repeats, the saved value is reused immediately.

Tabulation solves subproblems iteratively using tables, usually starting from the smallest cases and gradually building toward the final solution.

Both techniques reduce redundant computation and improve efficiency significantly.

sections.title: Studying for Exams Analogy
sections.content:
Imagine solving a difficult math problem repeatedly without writing down previous solutions.

Each time the same calculation appears, you would waste time recomputing it.

Instead, keeping notes allows you to reuse earlier work instantly.

Dynamic Programming follows this same principle by storing useful intermediate results.

sections.title: Dynamic Programming in Real Applications
sections.content:
Dynamic Programming is widely used in artificial intelligence, route optimization, financial systems, genetics, and machine learning.

Many advanced optimization problems rely on Dynamic Programming because it dramatically improves efficiency compared to brute force recursion.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Dynamic Programming improves efficiency by storing and reusing previously computed results. Techniques such as memoization and tabulation eliminate redundant calculations and optimize recursive problem solving.
